newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM alerts troops over Papua crisis.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM alerts troops over Papua crisis.

text.p: Australian troops have been placed on standby in case the crisis in neighbouring Papua New Guinea worsened, Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday.
Howard told reporters the move, made late on Thursday, was sensible in view of the situation in the South Pacific nationa, but did not mean Australia had decided to deploy troops.
"It was in response to a routine determination by the head of the Australian defence force.
"It was a normally prudent, senisble thing and it was a very sort of modest acceleration of the state of readiness."
Australia was Papua New Guinea's colonia administrator until the nation won independence in 1975.

Australia's top diplomat, who has spent two days in talks with Papua New Guinea Prime MInster Sir Julius Chan, was to brief Howard on the crisis later on Friday when he returned from Papua New Guinea.
"It's obviously still very unstable," Howard said.
"The impression is that things are domestically a little calmer today than what they were yesterday, but I don't want to emphasise that too strongly."

The worst crisis in PNG's 22-year history began on Monday when army chief Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok demanded that Chan quit over his hiring of mercenaries to put down an uprising on Bougainville island.

Singirok was promptly sacked but on Friday, holed up inside the Murray barracks, he repeated his demand and said Chan and two other senior ministers must quit before parliament sits again next Tuesday.
Singirok has consistently appealed for calm.
"The calming influence being exercised by the former head of the defence force, General Singirok is to be welcomed," Howard said.

Australian officials said the increased state of readiness applied to "some elements" of the military, but would not elaborate. But it was believed to involve parts of the Operational Deployment Force based at Townsville, in northern Queensland.
They and the Special Air Service Regiment at Perth, on the west coast, are the Australian Defence Force's highest readiness units, able to deploy overseas at short notice.
Thousands of Australians live and work in PNG.
